text: For several days. <break time="0.8s" /> We painted and read together. <break time="0.8s" /> Or I listened to the wild songs. <break time="0.8s" /> That he played upon his guitar. <break time="0.8s" /> But nothing could lighten his darkness. <break time="0.8s" /> One of these songs. <break time="0.8s" /> Which he called The Haunted Palace. <break time="0.8s" /> Told of a happy palace. <break time="0.8s" /> Whose king was overthrown by evil things. <break time="0.8s" /> Usher believed. <break time="0.8s" /> That the gray stones of his house. <break time="0.8s" /> Along with the still water beside it. <break time="0.8s" /> Had a kind of silent life. <break time="0.8s" /> Of their own. <break time="0.8s" /> This silent power. <break time="0.8s" /> He said. <break time="0.8s" /> Had shaped the fate of his family. <break time="0.8s" /> For centuries. <break time="0.8s" /> And had made him what he now was. <break time="0.8s" /> Having informed me abruptly one evening. <break time="0.8s" /> That the Lady Madeline was no more. <break time="0.8s" /> He said that he would keep her body. <break time="0.8s" /> For two weeks in a vault. <break time="0.8s" /> He explained. <break time="0.8s" /> That her disease had been unusual. <break time="0.8s" /> That her doctors were too curious about it. <break time="0.8s" /> And that the family burial ground was far away. <break time="0.8s" /> Together we carried the coffin. <break time="0.8s" /> Down into the deep, damp vault. <break time="0.8s" /> Which had long ago been used. <break time="0.8s" /> For storing gunpowder. <break time="0.8s" /> Only then did I notice. <break time="0.8s" /> How much they looked alike. <break time="0.8s" /> And Usher told me in a few words. <break time="0.8s" /> That he and his sister had been twins. <break time="0.8s" /> There was still a faint blush. <break time="0.8s" /> Upon her face. <break time="0.8s" /> And a strange, lingering smile. <break time="0.8s" /> Was on her lips.
